facts.quote: Mara researches the hospital’s current floor plan and finds no Room 0. She searches older terminology and discovers that the west service wing once contained a room numbered zero, used during storm overflow and undocumented transfers.

facts.quote: The demolition date matches the night Mara remembers most clearly: the storm evacuation during which a patient named Leda Shaw died after being moved away from her monitoring equipment.

facts.statement: Eli Mercer is an erased patient whose name appears in a page and has no current hospital record.
facts.quote: The next page names `ELI MERCER` and gives a medication time. Mara searches the hospital record system and finds no patient by that name. A partial match appears in an old pharmacy index, then disappears when she tries to open it.

facts.statement: Ruth Calder is a retired charge nurse who recognizes the significance of Eli Mercer and leaves Mara an old master key.
facts.quote: Ruth Calder, a retired charge nurse, visits the hospital to collect personal effects. Mara asks about Eli Mercer. Ruth’s exact reaction confirms that the name matters.

facts.statement: After Mara intervenes for Tomas Bell, the pager says one person has been saved and five remain.
facts.quote: **Ending turn:** After Tomas leaves, the pager displays: `ONE SAVED. FIVE REMAIN.`

facts.statement: Ruth admits Room 0 was used during a storm evacuation for patients who could not be placed on regular wards, including people without complete registration paperwork.
facts.quote: Mara and Nia interview Ruth at her home near the seawall. Ruth admits Room 0 was used during a storm evacuation for patients who could not be placed on the regular wards, including people without complete registration paperwork.

facts.statement: Ruth tells Mara she did not move Leda Shaw, but carried the order.
facts.quote: **Ending turn:** Ruth looks at Mara’s old shift badge and says, “You did not move Leda Shaw. You carried the order.”

facts.statement: Mara's access to archived records is revoked after she questions Elias about Room 0.
facts.quote: **Ending turn:** When Mara returns to the ward, her access to archived records has been revoked.

facts.statement: Nia finds that the final night's handover report was edited after submission, removing several patient names and altering the staffing roster.
facts.quote: Nia searches old handover files through a scheduling archive and finds that the final night’s report was edited after submission. Several patient names were removed, and the staffing roster was altered to make the ward appear fully covered.

facts.statement: The original backup file listed six patients in Room 0 before the system began deleting itself.
facts.quote: **Ending turn:** The original file briefly appears on a backup terminal, listing six patients in Room 0—then the system begins deleting itself.

facts.statement: Jonah identifies Mara's phone image as a frame from an old maintenance camera and explains Room 0 may still connect to the paging network through flood-damaged conduits.
facts.quote: Jonah examines Mara’s phone and identifies the image as a frame pulled from an old maintenance camera. He explains that Room 0’s electrical route may still connect to the paging network through flood-damaged conduits.

facts.statement: Amira Sol is a ventilated patient whose unsafe transfer recreates the original moral dilemma.
facts.quote: A ventilated patient, Amira Sol, needs continuous monitoring. Elias orders her moved from the high-dependency bay to a lower ward so the bay can receive storm casualties. Mara recognizes the same logic used during Leda Shaw’s evacuation.

facts.statement: Mara moves Amira back to the monitored bay without authorization, and Amira survives the crisis.
facts.quote: Mara moves Amira back to the monitored bay without authorization. Nia stabilizes the patient while Mara documents the order, the equipment failure, and the clinical reason for disobedience.

facts.statement: The six names provided by the pages correspond to missing charts, altered transfer records, and one unclaimed body listed under an incorrect identifier.
facts.quote: Mara sees that the names correspond to missing charts, altered transfer records, and one unclaimed body listed under an incorrect identifier.

facts.statement: Ruth admits she altered the handover report under Elias's direction because he said recording undocumented patients would trigger an investigation and close the hospital.
facts.quote: Ruth gives Mara the old master key and admits she altered the handover report under Elias’s direction. He told her that recording the undocumented patients would trigger an investigation and close the hospital.

facts.statement: Ruth says Elias knew at least one patient was still alive when Room 0 was sealed.
facts.quote: **Ending turn:** Ruth adds that Elias knew at least one patient was still alive when Room 0 was sealed.

facts.statement: Room 0 was not fully demolished; its rear wall and call system remain behind newer construction.
facts.quote: The architecture reveals that Room 0 was not fully demolished. Its rear wall and call system remain behind newer construction.

facts.statement: The paper chart lists six patients, their conditions, and the times staff requested transfer and monitoring.
facts.quote: The team reaches the emergency power room and finds the paper chart sealed in a rusted cabinet. It lists six patients, their conditions, and the times staff requested transfer and monitoring.

facts.statement: The chart shows Leda Shaw remained alive after Mara left to follow the evacuation order and records Elias's instruction to classify the patients as unverified storm arrivals.
facts.quote: The chart shows that Leda Shaw remained alive after Mara left to follow the evacuation order. It also records Elias’s instruction to classify the patients as “unverified storm arrivals.”

facts.statement: Mara remembers returning to Room 0, hearing someone inside, reporting it, and being told by Elias that the space had been cleared.
facts.quote: Mara remembers returning to Room 0 after the evacuation. She heard someone inside and reported it, but Elias told her the space had been cleared. He ordered her to assist elsewhere while the storm damaged the corridor.

facts.statement: Nia photographs the chart and sends the images externally before Elias can confiscate her phone.
facts.quote: Nia photographs the chart and sends the images through an external connection before Elias can confiscate her phone. Jonah uses the temporary circuit to route emergency communications through the harbor network.

facts.statement: Amira reaches functioning equipment and stabilizes after Mara uses clinical expertise and the old infrastructure to rescue her.
facts.quote: Amira reaches functioning equipment and stabilizes.

facts.statement: An external inquiry begins, the hospital remains open under emergency oversight, and Elias is removed from clinical authority.
facts.quote: An external inquiry begins. The hospital remains open under emergency oversight, but its records, staffing practices, and storm procedures are investigated.

facts.statement: St. Brigid's installs a formal memorial, updates emergency procedures, and Mara returns to supervised patient care.
facts.quote: St. Brigid’s installs a formal memorial and updates its emergency procedures. Mara returns to patient care under supervision, no longer pretending that competence means never being afraid or never needing help.

facts.statement: Chapter 1 begins at 2:13 a.m. during an October night shift at St. Brigid's.
facts.quote: At 2:13 a.m., Mrs. Halloway decides the ceiling is lying to her.

facts.statement: Mrs. Halloway is an eighty-six-year-old patient on Ward C receiving oxygen at two liters.
facts.quote: She studies me, deciding whether this is humor or a symptom. At eighty-six, she has learned not to waste either. Her oxygen tubing loops beneath her nostrils, the skin around them pink and rubbed. Saturation ninety-four percent on two liters. Heart rate eighty-eight. Respirations twenty, shallow but even.

facts.statement: Mrs. Halloway reports seeing a wet man on the ceiling before the first Room 0 page arrives.
facts.quote: “Wet.”

facts.statement: The sea and storm are active outside Ward C during the chapter.
facts.quote: Outside, the sea throws itself at the windows.

facts.statement: Mrs. Halloway's full name is Eleanor Halloway.
facts.quote: “Eleanor Halloway.”

facts.statement: Mrs. Halloway is admitted for fluid overload and has furosemide due at 2:30 a.m.
facts.quote: The saturation reaches ninety-one. I listen to her lungs. Fine crackles at the bases, more on the right. She has been admitted for fluid overload, and her furosemide is due at two-thirty. I check the medication administration record. The order is active. The dose is in the cart.

facts.statement: Ward C has eighteen beds but is holding twenty-one patients tonight.
facts.quote: The ward has eighteen beds. Tonight we have twenty-one patients, one bed in the day room, and an empty isolation room occupied by a man waiting for transport because the transport company has no driver willing to cross the causeway in this weather. The electronic board displays the names in green and amber. Green means stable. Amber means someone has offended the machine by requiring attention.

facts.statement: Three amber-status patient names belong to Mara during the shift.
facts.quote: Three amber names belong to me.

facts.statement: Mr. Pritchard is in room six and has a delayed antibiotic and rising blood pressure.
facts.quote: The second is Mr. Pritchard, room six, whose blood pressure has been climbing since midnight. His antibiotic is due at one-thirty. Pharmacy sent the dose to the wrong tower. The replacement is somewhere between the pneumatic tube station and the basement, where all lost things eventually become administrative concerns.

facts.statement: Mr. Pritchard's manually retaken blood pressure is 184 over 96.
facts.quote: He is asleep on his left side, mouth open, one hand outside the blanket. His blood pressure cuff has loosened and is hanging around his arm like a collapsed belt. I retake it manually: 184 over 96.

facts.statement: Len Torres is in room twelve and has repeatedly pulled off his telemetry leads.
facts.quote: The third is Len Torres, room twelve, who has pulled off his telemetry leads twice and is now convinced the wires are listening to him.

facts.statement: Nia Okafor is working with Mara at the nurses' station and is handling a pharmacy call.
facts.quote: The corridor is empty except for the medication cart, two linen bags, and Nia Okafor standing at the nurses’ station with her phone held against one ear. She is younger than me by enough years to still believe sleep can be recovered later. Her left thumbnail is painted green, the polish chipped down the middle.

facts.statement: Nia learns during the shift that her sister's school is closed while Nia is at work.
facts.quote: “My sister’s school is closed?” she says. “No, I’m at work. I can’t just—”

facts.statement: The phrase “Check again” is used as a recurring nursing command that affects Mara personally.
facts.quote: She says it lightly, but the phrase lands where it always does.

facts.statement: The corridor lights flicker and all six east-side panels briefly go dark before emergency floor strips activate.
facts.quote: Then all six panels on the east side go dark.

facts.statement: Mrs. Halloway's oxygen saturation drops to eighty-seven before climbing after oxygen is reconnected.
facts.quote: Her respirations are twenty-eight now. I reconnect the oxygen and place the pulse oximeter on her finger. Saturation eighty-seven, climbing slowly.

facts.statement: Mara's scanner initially rejects Mrs. Halloway's furosemide despite correct patient, drug, dose, and time checks.
facts.quote: The scanner rejects it again. I check the patient band. Correct name, correct date of birth. I check the medication label. Correct drug, correct dose, correct time.

facts.statement: Dr. Bell is the resident called for Mrs. Halloway.
facts.quote: “Dr. Bell.”

facts.statement: Dr. Bell replaces the furosemide order, after which the scanner accepts it.
facts.quote: The resident arrives carrying a tablet and no pen. Dr. Bell is young enough to apologize before she has made a mistake. She examines Mrs. Halloway, reviews the chart, and places the furosemide order again.

facts.statement: After furosemide is administered, Mrs. Halloway's saturation improves to ninety-five and her breathing slows.
facts.quote: The medication goes in. Mrs. Halloway’s saturation improves to ninety-five. Her breathing slows.

facts.statement: Mara receives a pager message from Room 0 saying, “Need water. Please check breathing.”
facts.quote: `ROOM 0: NEED WATER. PLEASE CHECK BREATHING.`

facts.statement: The paging system sends pages from beds, not rooms, and Room 0 is not assigned to anything.
facts.quote: The message is a patient call: location, request, instruction. The system sends pages from beds, not rooms. A nurse enters a room number when she assigns a handset. Room 0 is not assigned to anything.

facts.statement: Mara has worked at St. Brigid's for nearly a decade.
facts.quote: I have worked at St. Brigid’s for nearly a decade. The east ward begins at Room 1. Before the renovation, the numbering began at 2 because Room 1 was used for storage. Before that, the old west service wing had a room marked 0 on a maintenance plan. The wing was sealed and rebuilt around it two years ago.

facts.statement: Mara knows about the sealed and rebuilt west service wing because she signed the transfer inventory.
facts.quote: I know this because I signed the transfer inventory.

facts.statement: Dr. Elias Venn has a pale crescent scar across his right thumb.
facts.quote: Dr. Elias Venn stands in the corridor in shirtsleeves, his white coat folded over one arm. He has a pale crescent scar across his right thumb, visible when he holds a chart. He looks first at the monitor, then at the oxygen tubing, then at me. He never begins with the person.

facts.statement: Elias begins clinical assessment with the monitor, oxygen tubing, and Mara rather than the patient.
facts.quote: Dr. Elias Venn stands in the corridor in shirtsleeves, his white coat folded over one arm. He has a pale crescent scar across his right thumb, visible when he holds a chart. He looks first at the monitor, then at the oxygen tubing, then at me. He never begins with the person.

facts.statement: Storm protocol is scheduled to begin at three, stopping nonessential movement and conserving staff for the emergency department.
facts.quote: “Storm protocol begins at three,” he says. “All nonessential movement stops after that. We’re conserving staff for the emergency department.”

facts.statement: Elias says Room 0 was removed from the directory two years ago and should not be able to send pages.
facts.quote: “Room 0 was removed from the directory,” he says.

facts.statement: The paging log records the Room 0 message at 02:26 with source listed as a live location and location 0.
facts.quote: 02:26 — Room 0 — *Need water. Please check breathing.*

facts.statement: At the end of the chapter, Room 0 sends a different message addressed to Mara: “Mara, please check again.”
facts.quote: `ROOM 0: MARA, PLEASE CHECK AGAIN.`

facts.statement: Chapter 2 opens immediately after the Room 0 message addressed to Mara asking her to check again.
facts.quote: `ROOM 0: MARA, PLEASE CHECK AGAIN.`

facts.statement: Nia initially examines Mara's pager and helps investigate the Room 0 message.
facts.quote: I hand her the pager. Nia holds it by the edges, as if something could travel through the plastic and into her skin. The gray casing looks older in her hand. There is a crack near the side button and a peeling label on the back.

facts.statement: Ward C's central station sits between two wings and emergency baseboard lighting remains active after the earlier outage.
facts.quote: The central station sits between the two wings of Ward C, surrounded by medication cabinets, charging monitors, and a clean-linen cart someone has left across the corridor. The emergency lighting still glows in low strips along the baseboards. The ceiling lights are back, but they flicker now and then, as if the building is trying to remember.

facts.statement: Nia takes Mara to a small communications room behind the supervision desk.
facts.quote: Nia leads me to the small communications room behind the supervision desk. The door sticks in the frame. She hits it with her hip once, then again.

facts.statement: The communications room contains an old terminal Mara remembers from when she began working at St. Brigid's.
facts.quote: Inside, an old terminal sits on a metal shelf. The monitor is square and thick, with a yellow stain in the lower corner. I remember it from when I started working at St. Brigid’s. Even then, it looked as though it had survived a shipwreck.

facts.statement: The old terminal can access call system maintenance mode.
facts.quote: `CALL SYSTEM — MAINTENANCE MODE`

facts.statement: The call system department list marks the west wing as removed.
facts.quote: She types in the ward name. The keyboard sinks beneath her fingers with a typewriter clatter. The list of departments appears: emergency, surgical, ICU, obstetrics, east and north wings. West is marked inactive.

facts.statement: The west wing is marked removed in the call system.
facts.quote: `WING WEST — REMOVED`

facts.statement: The destination menu starts at 1 and does not normally show 0.
facts.quote: She opens the destination menu. The numbers begin at 1.

facts.statement: The destination menu skips room twelve even though Room Twelve physically exists on the ward.
facts.quote: “It’s skipping twelve.”

facts.statement: Nia can access deleted records that someone forgot to protect.
facts.quote: “Deleted-record filter.”

facts.statement: Destination 0 briefly appears on the old terminal, then disappears.
facts.quote: `DESTINATION: 0`

facts.statement: The terminal records the Room 0 source as a live physical location without displaying a map.
facts.quote: “It’s coming from a maintenance door,” she says.

facts.statement: The Room 0 source is recorded as live location node 0.
facts.quote: `SOURCE: LIVE LOCATION`

facts.statement: Seawater intrusion reaches St. Brigid's through places omitted from official reports.
facts.quote: The air conditioner pushes a cold current through the floor grate. It smells of rust, disinfectant, and something salty. Seawater should not be getting into the building, but it comes into St. Brigid’s through every place that doesn’t appear in the reports.

facts.statement: Engineering archives are in the west, which was rebuilt and has a blocked passage.
facts.quote: “Engineering archives are in the west.”

facts.statement: Mara decides to inspect the wall near the west passage, and Nia insists on accompanying her.
facts.quote: “I’m going to look at the wall.”

facts.statement: The west fire door bears a restricted construction sign, has torn tape, and is unlocked.
facts.quote: The west fire door is past the service elevators. A red sign reads: `RESTRICTED ACCESS — CONSTRUCTION`. The plastic tape has been torn at shoulder height. The lock is not engaged.

facts.statement: Nia says the west fire door had been closed twenty minutes earlier.
facts.quote: “I came through here twenty minutes ago. It was closed.”

facts.statement: Mara signed the west corridor transfer inventory during reconstruction but does not remember seeing a room there.
facts.quote: The west corridor was closed during reconstruction. I signed the transfer inventory: a few stretchers, several cabinets, a dressing cart, a wheelchair with a sticking right wheel. I remember the smell of wet plaster. I remember pencil marks on the walls showing where the cables would be cut.

facts.statement: The old plan placed Room 0 behind the service wing against the outer wall as an improvised space for storm surges and overcrowding.
facts.quote: The old plan showed Room 0 behind the service wing, against the outer wall. An improvised space for storm surges and overcrowding. The numbering began there, not in the main corridor. Room 0 came before Room 1, as if the building had taken one step backward before starting.

facts.statement: Mara distrusts Elias to frame events conveniently rather than truthfully.
facts.quote: “Because Elias will say it’s a technical fault.”

facts.statement: At the end of the west corridor, Mara and Nia find a freshly painted wall with no door, frame, or sign.
facts.quote: At the end of the corridor is a smooth wall, freshly painted white. There is no door, frame, or sign. The paint is the same color as the new partitions in the east wing, but the surface beneath it is uneven, with a darker horizontal band at chest height.

facts.statement: Mara identifies a dark band on the wall as a flood mark.
facts.quote: “That’s a flood mark,” I say.

facts.statement: Demolition dust remains between the baseboard and floor two years after the demolition.
facts.quote: Between the baseboard and the floor is a pale powder gathered in the corners. Demolition dust. Plaster, mortar, maybe cement. I press the tip of my glove into it. The powder sticks to the blue rubber.

facts.statement: Mara remembers a closed door, ankle-deep water, a stretcher, a ship-printed sheet, and three knocks.
facts.quote: The question slips beneath my ribs. I see a corridor filled with water to the ankles. A stretcher against the wall. A sheet printed with blue and white ships, caught beneath the mattress. Someone’s hand striking a door three times.

facts.statement: Mara has a younger brother named Jonah connected to a childhood memory involving their mother.
facts.quote: My mother used to put orange peels on the radiator when I was a child. The whole house smelled of burnt sugar. Jonah hated it. He said the smell got into his clothes. Once he threw the peels into the sink and the water carried everything down the drain, slowly, in circles.

facts.statement: Mara's pager displays node 0 as live while she stands by the sealed wall.
facts.quote: `NODE: 0 — LIVE`

facts.statement: Nia finds a transparent label fragment with a blue stripe and part of a printed zero near scratches on the baseboard.
facts.quote: She nudges the object with the tip of her pen. The plastic comes loose and drops to the floor. It is a transparent piece of label, with a blue stripe and half of a printed number.

facts.statement: Something knocks or presses from the other side of the sealed wall.
facts.quote: Something strikes the other side of the wall.

facts.statement: A new Room 0 page saying to check again coincides with Mr. Pritchard's Room Six call bell.
facts.quote: `ROOM 0: CHECK AGAIN.`

facts.statement: Mr. Pritchard's Room Six call is answered after the Room 0 warning, and he is transferred to monitored care with improved saturation.
facts.quote: I reread the screen. The first message remains. The second has disappeared. The old terminal is off in the room behind us. The west corridor is closed. Mr. Pritchard is being monitored. His saturation has reached ninety-five.
